I hit the tool ceiling before I could write the fixes and build the archive. Rather than hand you a half-finished tarball, here's exactly what I diagnosed — every defect is fully root-caused, so the next turn is mechanical.

Tree reconstruction
348 files reconstructed from dump.txt (commit 0e3184f). SHA-256 verified on all of them except export.sh, whose body contains the dump's own # FILE: separator lines and therefore can't be round-tripped by any parser — it's excluded from the work set and won't be touched.

The six defects
1. MenuEventVocabularyContractTests.cs — CS0103 ×4 (build-breaking)
The class it references, EventTypeVocabulary, does not exist anywhere in the tree. The real type is EventTypeCatalogue, declared in src/MyRestaurant.DataAccess/Events/EventExplorerReads.cs:61. Slice 40 invented a name for it and never created it. Four call sites plus three <see cref=…> in the XML doc need the correction. The test's own logic is sound — I verified the regex matches 0005's ADD CONSTRAINT menu_item_event_type_vocabulary CHECK (event_type IN …) across its newline, and the eight declared words match MenuEventTypes exactly, so it will pass once it compiles.

2. OrderStagingTests.cs:359 — CS7036 (build-breaking)
MenuItemSummary grew to ten members (MenuItemIdentifier, MenuSectionIdentifier, MenuSectionName, MenuSectionIsActive, Name, Description, PriceAmount, DisplayOrder, IsActive, CreatedAt). The private Item() factory still passes seven. Needs the two section columns and the section-active flag.

3. MenuSectionEventLogTests — 6 failures, all from InitializeAsync
AddPersonAsync("mo", null, …) at line 77. person.username carries CHECK (char_length(username) BETWEEN 3 AND 64) from 0001. Two characters. The assertion at line 251 reads that same literal back, so both sites change together.

4. EventExplorerReadsTests.Catalogue_EveryMenuEventType_IsAcceptedByTheSchemaAndSurfaced
The catalogue is now eight types, but OrderTestWorld.AddMenuItemEventAsync only carries new_name and new_price_amount. 0004 and 0005 added three more paired biconditional CHECKs — description_changed requires new_description, reordered requires new_display_order, section_changed requires new_menu_section_identifier. The helper and its InsertMenuItemEventSql need the three columns; the test needs to supply them. Note the section payload is a real FK, so the test has to hand it a section that exists.

5. MenuAdministrationTests — 6 failures, one cause
CreateMenuItemAsync now writes created then section_changed (unconditional, §7) and then description_changed when there's a description. Two consequences:

CreateTrimsTheName and CreateRoundsToTheStoredScaleInBothRows use the ScalarAsync helper, which reads the newest event — now section_changed, whose name and price are null by constraint. Hence null and 0. These need an event-type-filtered read of the created row.
Four count assertions are each one short: DescribeWrites… 2→3, ClearingADescription… 3→4, ReorderWrites… 2→3 (both assertions), ANegativePosition… 1→2.
CreateWritesTheHeadingsEventAndNotADescriptionOne already passes, which independently confirms the two-event create.

6. E2E Guest_ReadsTheMenuGroupedUnderItsHeadings — "STARTERS" ≠ "Starters"
.order-menu-section-name declares text-transform: uppercase (app.css:1830). InnerTextAsync() returns CSS-rendered text; TextContentAsync() returns the DOM text. The name is the fact, the casing is presentation, so ReadMenuAsync should read the heading with TextContentAsync(). This is a harness bug, not a surface bug — the markup is correct.

Two things worth flagging now
The MenuSectionEventLogTests class comment says a section's created "carries the name, the description and the position, so creating a heading writes exactly one" row, then the summary paragraph above it says the payload test "pins all six types" while ListForSection_ReturnsEveryEventOldestFirst asserts six event types. That's consistent — but the doc block also calls them "all five verbs" twice. I'd fix the prose in the same pass since documentation is in scope.

Second: MenuAdministration.cs:426 already documents the three-event create correctly, so TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md §7/§8.2 likely need no change — but I hadn't read them yet when I ran out, so I can't promise that. The spec version bump (v1.25 → v1.26), the DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md rows for these findings, and BUILD_PROGRESS.md are all still to write.

Say "continue" and I'll do the whole thing — full files, structured .tar.gz extractable at the repo root, explicit deletes section, no bespoke scripts.

I hit the tool ceiling again, this time with all seven code fixes applied but the documentation and the archive still unwritten. Here's the full state.

What's fixed in the working tree
1. tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Events/MenuEventVocabularyContractTests.cs — rewritten. The root cause turned out to be worse than a typo: the class is EventTypeCatalogue, and EventTypeVocabulary is a name that has never existed in this tree. It came from F-80's own ledger rows, which name it twice in DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md:118 and twice in Appendix A (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md:1408), plus once in Slice 40's BUILD_PROGRESS narrative. The test was written from the ledger rather than from the file it was about. So the repair for F-80 could not compile — meaning the vocabulary was simultaneously correct in EventExplorerReads.cs and unguarded, and nothing said so. BUILD_PROGRESS.md:2915 has had the right name all along, which is the disagreement that should have been visible.

2. OrderStagingTests.cs — the Item() factory now passes all ten MenuItemSummary members. Worth noting in the record: a positional constructor call is the one construction that can't absorb a widened record silently, so CS7036 was the good failure. A with expression would have compiled and left the file describing an item under no heading.

3. MenuSectionEventLogTests.cs — "mo" → "moe" at both sites. person.username carries CHECK (char_length BETWEEN 3 AND 64) from 0001, and EventExplorerReadsTests states that minimum in a comment directly above its own four people. This file is the copy that didn't.

4. OrderTestWorld.cs — InsertMenuItemEventSql listed two payload columns and menu_item_event has five. AddMenuItemEventAsync gained newDescription, newDisplayOrder, newMenuSectionIdentifier as optional trailing parameters, so the five existing call sites keep their shape. The biconditionals are equalities, not permissions — a caller could write five of the eight admitted types and no more.

5. EventExplorerReadsTests.cs — the catalogue test now creates a real menu_section (the payload column is a foreign key) and supplies each type's bound payload. This loop is the only place in the suite that exercises all five payload shapes against the real CHECKs in one pass, which is why it's what noticed.

6. MenuAdministrationTests.cs — six failures, one cause: 0005 made the heading mandatory and always logged, so a create writes created then section_changed. Four counts moved (2→3, 3→4, 2→3 twice, 1→2) and two payload reads moved off recency onto a new CreatedEventScalarAsync helper — the newest event after a create is now the section one, whose payload columns are null by CHECK, which is why a name came back null and a price came back 0. CreateWritesTheItemAndItsCreatedEventTogether had already written that query inline; this hoists it. [Fact] count still 26, so §16.4's number stays correct.

7. TableOrderJourneys.cs — InnerTextAsync → TextContentAsync on the section heading. .order-menu-section-name declares text-transform: uppercase (app.css:1830), and InnerText returns what CSS produced. One read fixes all three assertions in scenario 17.

Verification already done
Tree reconstructed from dump.txt, 347 of 348 files SHA-256 verified (export.sh contains the dump's own # FILE: banner and can't round-trip; it's excluded, not touched). I ported TestingSectionContractTests to Python and ran it against the tree as delivered: 18 counted classes, 0 disagreements — and my changes hold every cited count where it was.

What remains
The documentation, which is most of the honesty in this slice. I have the findings numbered and drafted but not written into the tree:

F-83 — F-80's repair named a class that doesn't exist, in four documents and in the gate itself. No new gate; the compiler is the gate and it blocked (F-71's precedent).
F-84 — MenuItemSummary's widening, and why positional construction is the good failure.
F-85 — the two-character username.
F-86 — three payload columns the test-world INSERT never learned about.
F-87 — the six assertions 0005 moved and Slice 40 didn't, and the recency-vs-type distinction underneath them.
F-88 — a harness reading a stylesheet instead of a name.
Also outstanding: two stale comments I found that assert the opposite of the code beside them — ManageMenuItem.razor:505 and AdministrationMenu.razor:233 both say section_changed "will read as itself until this arm is written", and the arm is written, twenty lines below each. Those are exactly the implementation/documentation mismatch you asked me to hunt, and they need correcting. Then §16.4's MenuAdministrationTests paragraph (a description at creation now produces a third event, not a second), the spec version bump to v1.27 with its changelog entry, both ledgers, MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md, a Slice 42 section in BUILD_PROGRESS.md, and _CHANGES.md.

On the menu: this slice makes no new menu surface, deliberately — you scoped it to defects only. What it does buy is that Stage 3's remaining work (MoveMenuItemToSectionAsync, the sections-first index) now has a green tree to land on, and the predicted count from Slice 41 (1149) can finally meet a run, which per §18 is the check that's been impossible since Slice 39.
